data.narrative:
Compound Eye is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $20.6M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a peer set of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and Nimble Robotics—supplemented by a broader comp universe of 8 private firms and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier to the $21M raised proxy, implying a $39M valuation. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against the four core comparables, which traded at a median valuation of $1.6B (range: $1.0B–$1.8B), directly implying $1.6B. The stage-progression method reflects early-stage valuation discipline; the peer-median method reflects market pricing for proven robotics businesses at similar or slightly later stages.

The triangulated analysis yields a low of $33M, median of $832M, and high of $1.9B. The wide range reflects meaningful uncertainty about whether Compound Eye's current progress and market position align closer to the stage-progression baseline or to late-stage peer valuations. Key drivers of this spread include capital efficiency relative to peers, product commercialization progress, and addressable market defensibility. Resolution typically comes through Series B fundraising outcomes and operational milestones.
